app.name: Mihrab
app.tagline: Prayer times focused on Sweden — with sources tuned for Swedish cities and flexible options elsewhere.

a11y.countdownHere: The countdown is set to this prayer. Tap to go back to the next one.

home.monthTimesLink: Prayer times for the whole month
home.localFallbackNotice: On-device calculation — connect to refresh from your provider
home.lastGpsCoordsNotice: Using last known location — GPS unavailable
home.exactAlarmDenied: Prayer alerts need exact-alarm permission for accurate timing. Tap to grant.
home.notifPermDenied: Notification permission denied — prayer alerts won't fire. Tap to open Settings.
home.alertOverrideA11y: {{prayer}} is set to {{mode}} just this once
home.timezoneShiftNotice: The clocks here changed ({{from}} → {{to}}). Prayer times have been refreshed.

errors.locationNeededBody: Prayer times use your approximate position. Grant location access in system settings, then try again.
errors.gpsPermission: Location permission is required to use device location.

month.locationNotReadyBody: Open Home and load today's times once so this screen can use your GPS position.
month.daruriLegend: The small line under Fajr, ʿAṣr and ʿIshāʾ is when each one's first (preferred) time ends. Ẓuhr's ends when ʿAṣr begins and Maghrib's when ʿIshāʾ does, so those two are the columns themselves. Fajr's and ʿAṣr's are approximate.

share.footerNote: Calculated times. Follow your local mosque where it differs.
share.pitch: Free and ad-free. Prayer times, qibla, the Qur’an with recitation and translation, and a khatmah tracker.

settings.colourThemeHelp: Classic keeps the app’s own paper and ink. Pick a colour to theme dark mode in it — light mode stays classic.
settings.themeHelp: System matches your device light or dark mode. Turn on System colors to use the platform palette in the app (including Material You on Android). Buttons and accents follow your phone’s primary color so the app matches your wallpaper when dynamic color is available.
settings.clockFormatHelp: Automatic follows your device's own clock setting. Prayer times, the month table and your widgets all use the same format.
settings.systemDynamicColorsHelp: Uses your device’s semantic and dynamic colors in the app, whichever theme you pick. Pure black (OLED) still darkens backgrounds when dark mode is on.
settings.pureBlackHelp: True black background in dark mode for OLED displays.
settings.providerAutoHelp: In Sweden, prayer times use the Sweden source (listed cities); outside Sweden, AlAdhan. Pick a source below to lock one provider.
settings.providerOverridden: {{picked}} has no times for where you are, so {{used}} is answering instead.
settings.manualSearchHelp: Tap a search result to apply it right away, or edit coordinates and press Apply below.
settings.calcHiddenSweden: Sweden uses prayer times per listed city. Your position is reverse-geocoded to match that city; only for Sweden.
settings.calcHiddenPraytimes: PrayTimes.dev applies its own published rules (see prayertimes.dev). Only madhab / Asr school applies here; method list is hidden.
settings.prayerAlertsHelp: Scheduled for the five daily prayers (Fajr–Isha). Android may require exact-alarm access for reliable timing.
settings.prePrayerReminderHelp: Optional second notification before each prayer.
settings.liveActivityHelp: Pinned countdown to the next prayer, with today's other times in the expanded view.
settings.liveActivityCompactHelp: Show only the countdown; hide the prayer list.
settings.languageHelp: Select the app language. Arabic and Urdu use right-to-left layout.
settings.widgetConfigureHint: You can also touch and hold the widget → settings (gear) to adjust the same options on Android.
settings.adhanAlarmStreamHelp: Uses the alarm volume, so the adhan is heard even when the phone is on silent or vibrate. Does not override Do Not Disturb.
settings.prayerAlertFullScreenHelp: When the phone is locked, each prayer's alert fills the screen like an alarm, so you can stop it, snooze it or log the prayer right there. The sound stays as chosen above.
settings.prayerAlertFullScreenBlocked: Full-screen alerts are off for Mihrab
settings.prayerAlertFullScreenBlockedHelp: Android shows an ordinary notification instead. Tap to allow full-screen alerts.
settings.notificationSoundDefaultHelp: Uses your device default notification sound.
settings.notificationSoundVoiceHelp: Built-in voice included in this app build.
settings.notificationSoundCustomHelp: Choose an audio file from this device.
settings.notificationSoundCustomTrimmed: Notifications play the first 30 seconds; the full recording plays when the app is open.
settings.prayerOffsetsHelp: Nudge each prayer by ±{{max}} minutes to match your local mosque.
settings.replayOnboardingHelp: Revisit your location, school, alerts and the rest.
settings.attributionsBlurb: Whose work this app is made of
settings.accentColorHelp: Used across the app and the home-screen widget.
settings.tintedSurfacesHelp: Use your accent color as the app's main color — across every screen, and on the home-screen widgets, Live Activity and prayer notifications. Off keeps the accent as a quiet highlight.
settings.verdantThemeHelp: Colors every surface in your chosen accent. Custom hex is unavailable — pick from the six presets.
settings.verdantThemeSystemDisabled: A colour theme is active — choose Classic to use system colours.
settings.widgetColorFollowsAccentHelp: The widget uses the same accent color as the app. Pick it under Appearance.
settings.widgetColorOwnHelp: The app is following your system colors, which the widget does not. Pick the widget’s highlight here.
settings.additionalTimesBlurb: Sunrise, midnight and the thirds of the night
settings.additionalTimesFooter: These appear in the prayer table, the widget and the Live Activity as well as in notifications, and they use the default sound rather than the adhan.
settings.dailyRemindersBlurb: An ayah each day, today's khatmah portion, Al-Kahf and Al-Mulk
settings.sunriseTimeHelp: Show sunrise in the prayer table, notifications, widget, and Live Activity.
settings.islamicMidnightHelp: The midpoint of the night between Maghrib and Fajr. Off by default.
settings.lastThirdHelp: The start of the last third of the night — the time for Qiyam al-Layl. Off by default.
settings.firstThirdHelp: The end of the first third of the night — in the Maliki reckoning, where Isha leaves its preferred window. Off by default.
settings.malikiSecondTimesHelp: Each prayer gets a line on the Today card saying when its preferred time (ikhtiyari) closes and its late time (daruri) begins. Computed on your device from your coordinates, whichever source your times come from. Uses the 1:1 shadow for Asr regardless of your madhab setting, because that is the Maliki boundary. Off by default.
settings.malikiSecondTimesHanafiWarning: Heads up: these are Maliki boundaries, but your Asr is set to Hanafi, which uses a different shadow. Zuhr's first time will end about half an hour before the Asr shown below it. Turn off Hanafi Asr if you want the card to agree with itself.
settings.malikiSecondTimesSource: From Al-Murshid al-Muin (Ibn Ashir), as rendered in The Guiding Helper, Song 11.
settings.malikiAlertsHelp: Off for every prayer to begin with. Pick only the ones you want to be told about — five more alerts a day is how an app teaches you to ignore it. Needs notifications turned on.
settings.malikiAlertsDisabled: Turn on the Maliki second times under Prayer times, and they can be announced here.
settings.malikiAlertsLeadTitle: Warn me before the first time ends
settings.malikiSecondTimesModelled: Fajr's and Asr's boundaries are the stars fading and the sun yellowing — an angle standing in for something the eye judges. They are marked as approximate. Where the sun does not rise, does not set, or never reaches the angle, nothing is shown rather than a guess.
settings.ayahOfDayHelp: A randomly chosen ayah with its translation, every day.
settings.khatmahReminderHelp: Today's portion and where to continue, while a khatmah is active.
settings.khatmahReminderNoPlan: Start a khatmah in the Qur’an tab to use this.
settings.resetAppHelp: Erase all settings and data. Cannot be undone.
settings.batteryWarningHelp: Battery optimization can delay or silence adhan alerts while the app is closed. Tap to exclude Mihrab.
settings.themeRestartManualBody: iOS does not allow apps to restart themselves. Please force-quit Prayer Times and reopen it for the new theme to take effect.
settings.liquidGlassHelp: Adopt iOS system colours and translucent glass chrome. Follows Light/Dark automatically.
settings.themeRestartBody: Switching system colors needs the app to restart so every screen picks up the new theme. Restart now?
settings.laLockButtonHelp: Show a button on the card for hiding it from the lock screen and always-on display.
settings.resetBody: This wipes all settings, saved locations, journal entries, fasting log, and tasbih state, then takes you back to the onboarding flow. This cannot be undone.
settings.endOfDayLogHelp: Ten minutes after Isha, asks whether to log the day’s five prayers. Answering it the next morning still logs the right day.
settings.alertModeHint: Changes how this prayer alerts you
settings.sectionNotificationsBlurb: Sounds, advance reminders, extra times, live activity
settings.sectionLocationBlurb: Where you are, and your saved places
settings.malikiRows: Show them in the day’s times
settings.malikiRowsHelp: Off, the boundaries are only announced — nothing is added to the card or the month.
settings.malikiEndAlertsHelp: A second notification at the moment the prayer becomes qada. Fired at the time itself, never early.
settings.madhabHelp: Shafii, Maliki and Hanbali take the same asr shadow, so choosing between them changes no time. Maliki also names the dawn prayer Subh and offers the second times.
settings.laDesignNeedsAndroid16: Styles need Android 16 or newer. This phone shows the standard card: the prayer, the time left and a progress bar.
settings.accentPickerAdjusted: Moved to the nearest shade that stays readable on this background.
settings.sectionAppearanceBlurbAndroid: Theme, accent, time format, language, widget
settings.verdantAccentHelp: Verdant colors every surface in this accent.
settings.refreshStoredHelp: Fetches this month again rather than filling the gaps, so times that are wrong — after a change of clocks, say — are replaced rather than kept.
settings.silenceToggle: Silence the phone at prayer time
settings.silenceHelp: Turns on Do Not Disturb around the prayers you choose, so the phone stays quiet in the mosque, and turns it off again afterwards. Alarms and whatever you allow through Do Not Disturb still get through.
settings.silenceAccessNeeded: Mihrab needs Do Not Disturb access to do this.
settings.silenceJumuahFixedHelp: Many mosques hold Jumu'ah at the same time all year. Off, the window follows Dhuhr.
settings.helpMihrabBlurb: Rate it, tell people about it, share a month of prayer times.

locationSetup.headline: Set your location
locationSetup.sub: Prayer times depend on where you are. Choose one of the options below — you can change this later in Settings.
locationSetup.manualSub: Search and tap a result to finish — or type latitude and longitude below and press Continue.

provider.autoSub: Sweden source in Sweden; AlAdhan elsewhere.
provider.autoNow: Where you are now, that is {{label}}.
provider.outOfRegion: No times for where you are — {{fallback}} would be used instead.
provider.footer: Country-specific sources use official or national prayer tables where we integrate them. More regions may be added over time.

prayertimes_dev.name: PrayTimes.dev

local_adhan.desc: Calculated on your phone with Batoul Adhan — no network prayer API.
local_adhan.name: On-device (Adhan JS)

islamiska_forbundet.desc: Prayer times for listed Swedish cities; your location is matched to the nearest city in the list.
islamiska_forbundet.name: Sweden

habous.name: Morocco

compass.needLocationBody: Set a location in Settings or open Home once with GPS so we can compute the Qibla direction.
compass.hint: Hold the phone flat and move away from metal. Align the Qibla arrow with “Phone front” when you face the Qibla.
compass.signalHelp: Based on magnetic field level and stability. Move away from metal and electronics if it stays low.
compass.signalWeakBody: Move away from metal, magnets, and electronics. Remove magnetic phone accessories, then make a slow figure-8 motion to recalibrate.
compass.motionDetectedBody: Too much movement can make direction jump. Hold the phone flat and still for a few seconds, away from moving vehicles or speakers.
compass.motionPermissionDeniedBody: Compass access is denied on iOS. Allow Motion & Fitness access in system settings, then reopen this screen.
compass.unsupportedBody: This device does not provide a usable magnetometer (or access failed). The live compass is turned off. Use the bearing below with a physical compass or map.
compass.checkingCompassWithPrompt: Starting compass… If prompted on iOS, allow Motion & Fitness access.
compass.a11yDialLive: Qibla compass. Rotate {{deg}} degrees to face Qibla.
compass.a11yDialChecking: Qibla compass. Waiting for sensor data.
compass.a11ySignal_weak: Compass signal: weak. Try moving to an open area.
compass.a11ySignal_very_weak: Compass signal: very weak. Accuracy may be limited.
compass.crossCheckBody: Your device's own compass is tuned to its hardware. For the most accurate reading, open it and turn until it shows {{degrees}}.

placeSearch.hint: Results from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim). Use respectfully — not for bulk geocoding.

quran.comingSoon: Full text for this surah will arrive in a future data update.
quran.mushafDownloadBody: The Madinah mushaf is around {{size}} MB. It is not bundled in the app — download it once and the pages stay cached on your device.
quran.mushafDownloadReadHint: Pages appear as they arrive; the rest downloads in the background.
quran.mushafDownloadRetryBody: {{count}} pages did not download. Retry to fetch the missing pages — everything already downloaded is kept.
quran.downloadSurahAudioShort: Download this surah for offline listening
quran.hideModeActive: Memorization mode: {{what}} hidden — tap an ayah to reveal
quran.noBookmarks: No bookmarks yet — tap any ayah while reading to bookmark or star it.
quran.shareAsImageHelp: A card with the ayah on it
quran.shareWithTafsirHelp: The ayah and {{edition}}, instead of the translation
quran.riwayahReflowBody: This mushaf starts and ends every page exactly where the printed one does, but its lines are laid out by your device rather than taken from the print, so they will not always break in the same places.
quran.riwayahNeedsHttps: The link must start with https://
quran.riwayahTooLarge: That file is much larger than a mushaf dataset. Check the link.
quran.riwayahUnreachable: Could not reach that link. Check the address and your connection.
quran.riwayahGotAPage: That link returned a web page, not a data file. Use the download link for the JSON export.
quran.riwayahNotJson: That file is not a data file.
quran.riwayahNotAQuran: That file is not a complete Qur’an, so it was not installed.
quran.riwayahCouldNotSave: Could not save it to this device.
quran.tafsirUnavailable: Tafsir unavailable — connect to the internet once to download it.
quran.khatmahResetTodayHelp: Rewinds only the pages recorded today.
quran.khatmahResetAllHelp: Back to where the plan began, with a fresh schedule.
quran.khatmahReminderBody: Today's portion: {{pages}} pages — continue from page {{page}}.
quran.khatmahMoveDateA11y: Change the date this khatmah is paced to
quran.khatmahPerDayToFinish: {{count}} pages a day to finish on time
quran.khatmahPaceNow: That is {{count}} pages a day now.
quran.tafsirEditionHelp: The commentary shown under each verse. Also changeable from any verse on the Quran page.
quran.companionHelp: Applies everywhere a verse is shown — the reader, the verse of the day, and the daily-ayah notification. Also changeable from any verse.
quran.mushafReplaceOldBody: An older copy of the mushaf ({{size}} MB) is still on your device from a previous version. It will be removed first — nothing you have saved is affected.
quran.shareAsTextHelp: The ayah, your translation and the reference
quran.shareChoiceA11y: Share — opens a choice of text or image card
quran.downloadChannelDesc: Progress while the Quran is downloading.
quran.audioDownloadDoneBody: The whole Quran in this voice is on this device. It plays without a connection now.
quran.audioDownloadIncompleteBody: {{count}} ayahs are still missing. Start it again to pick up where it stopped.
quran.tilawahBlurb: Recitation of the Quran — it keeps playing with the screen off, and works offline once downloaded.
quran.listenDownloadBody: The whole Quran in this voice, about {{size}}. The reader plays the same files, so this works there too.
quran.listenDownloadBusy: Something else is downloading. One at a time, so neither is halved.
quran.downloadDoneBody: Every page is on this device. It reads without a connection now.
quran.downloadIncompleteBody: {{count}} pages are still missing. Open the Quran to pick up where it stopped.
quran.riwayahSettingsHelp: Which muṣḥaf the reader draws. Ḥafṣ is built in; Warsh, Qālūn and Shuʿbah are downloaded once and can be removed again. Your place, your bookmarks and your khatmah are kept in verses, so they follow you from one to another.
quran.surahAudioPartial: {{have}} of {{total}} ayahs · tap to download the rest
quran.audioGap: {{surah}} {{ayah}} is not downloaded — connect, or download this surah for offline use.
quran.khatmahPrevDayHelp: Undo today’s mark and step back to the previous day’s portion.
quran.surahDownloadDoneBody: {{name}}’s recitation of {{surah}} is on this device. It plays without a connection now.
quran.verseByVerseHelp: Off, a surah opens as the mushaf and stays there. On, it can also be read as a list of verses with the translation under each one, and the reader’s header carries a button to move between the two.
quran.keepAwakeHelp: Holds the screen on while a surah, the mushaf or Tilawah is open, and lets go the moment you leave — so following the verses with the recitation playing does not mean tapping the screen to keep it lit. Your phone’s own screen timeout is left alone.
quran.khatmahGapOpen: Read the {{count}} pages left unread on day {{day}}
quran.khatmahGapOpen_one: Read the page left unread on day {{day}}
quran.khatmahGapOpenMany: Read the {{count}} pages left unread behind you
quran.khatmahGapOpenMany_one: Read the page left unread behind you
quran.newBookmarksHelp: A bookmark that follows moves along as you read, so it is where you stopped; a fixed one stays on the ayah you put it on. This sets what a new bookmark starts as — each bookmark keeps its own switch in the Bookmarks list.
quran.dayStartHelp: The Islamic day begins at sunset, so an evening of reading counts towards the day that has just begun and a session that runs past midnight stays one day. Off, days are counted from midnight. This changes the khatmah’s daily portion only — the prayer table still turns after the last time of the day.
quran.markPageUnread: Mark this page as not read
quran.khatmahPacingDateHelp: By {{date}} — what is left is re-cut every morning. Move it, or go back to a number of days.
quran.khatmahPacingDaysHelp: A length rather than a date, so the portions wait for you. Change it, or finish by a date instead.
quran.khatmahPacingHelp: A khatmah is paced either by a length — the portions wait for you — or by a date, which re-cuts what is left over the days that remain. You can move between the two at any point; nothing you have read is affected.
quran.khatmahPacingNone: Start a khatmah on the Quran page and how it is paced — a number of days, or a date to finish by — can be changed here.
quran.downloadStoppedBodyAyahs: {{done}} of {{total}} ayahs kept. Tap to continue, or it resumes by itself on Wi-Fi.
quran.downloadStoppedBodyPages: {{done}} of {{total}} pages kept. Tap to continue, or it resumes by itself on Wi-Fi.
quran.wordReaderBlurb: Hold a word in the mushaf to hear it on its own
quran.wordReader: Read a word on long press
quran.wordReaderHelp: In the mushaf, hold a finger on a word and nothing happens until you lift it: then that one word is read out. While holding, slide to another word to pick it instead. A long press no longer opens the verse — a tap still does.
quran.wordReaderReciterHelp: Only reciters with word timings can read a single word, so only they are listed. Your recitation reciter is separate and can be anyone.
quran.wordReaderOffline: That word is not on this device yet, and there is no connection to fetch it.
quran.wordReaderNoTiming: No timing is known for that word, so it cannot be read on its own.
quran.featuresOfferBody: Two things are off until you ask for them. Both can be changed later in Settings → Quran.
quran.featuresOfferTajweedNote: The coloured pages download in the background over Wi‑Fi, about 170 MB.
quran.verseOfDaySettingHelp: Shows a verse at the top of the Quran page, with its translation or tafsir, changing each day. The daily-ayah notification is separate — see Notifications.
quran.bookmarkShortcut: Shown under Continue reading on the Quran page
quran.homeBookmarkHelp: Quran page puts a bookmark under Continue reading at the top of this page. The star puts one bookmark on the Home screen, in the place a khatmah would take; only one bookmark can have it.
quran.homeBookmarkHelpKhatmah: Quran page puts a bookmark under Continue reading at the top of this page. The star puts one bookmark on the Home screen where Continue khatmah is — it is off while a khatmah is running.
quran.khatmahIntro: A khatmah is a reading of the whole muṣḥaf, cut into a portion a day. The app keeps your place, counts the pages, and says each day what is left.
quran.bookmarkColorInUse: Bookmark color {{color}} — in use at {{ref}}; tapping moves that bookmark here
quran.bookmarkColourReuseHelp: Off, each colour is one bookmark: choosing a colour that is already on another verse moves that bookmark. On, a colour can be used again and again — for every passage of one kind, say.
quran.bookmarkTapToRemove: Tap its colour again to remove
quran.bookmarkCircledHint: A ringed colour is on another ayah — picking it moves that bookmark here.
quran.khatmahPinnedHere: Your khatmah is at this ayah

listenAgain.heading: Carry on, or start something new
listenAgain.resumeSub: From ayah {{ayah}}, where you stopped listening
listenAgain.shuffleSub: A surah at random, then another

mosques.noneFound: No mosques found nearby. Try expanding the search radius.
mosques.needLocation: Set a location first so we can search nearby.
mosques.error: Couldn't reach the mosque database. Please try again.
mosques.title: Find a mosque near you
mosques.bodyWithLocation: We will open your maps app with a "mosque" search centered on your location. If your maps app is not available, we will open Google Maps in your browser.
mosques.bodyNoLocation: Set a location first (Settings → Location). We will then open your maps app with a "mosque" search centered on it. If your maps app is not available, we will open Google Maps in your browser.

journal.encourageEmpty: Mark today's first prayer to begin your journal.
journal.encourageActive: Every prayer logged is a step forward.
journal.notificationToggleOn: Tap "Log prayer" on the prayer-time alert to jump straight here.
journal.notificationToggleOff: Add a "Log prayer" action to each prayer-time alert.
journal.notificationToggleA11y: Enable journal log action on prayer notifications
journal.loadFailedBody: Your data is safe on disk but could not be read right now. Please try opening the journal again.

sync.pairIntro: Sync keeps your record the same on every device you use. It is peer to peer: your devices exchange encrypted files with each other, with no account and no server of ours, and only your own devices can read them.
sync.thisDeviceHelp: Show this code to your other device, or type it in there. It is not a password — it is safe to copy, photograph or send to yourself.
sync.addDeviceHelp: Type or paste the code shown on your other device.
sync.pairWarnBody: Everything recorded on that device will appear here, and everything here will appear there. Where the two disagree, the more recent entry is kept — and what you delete on one device is removed from the other too.
sync.pairedBody: This device has written its key to the folder. Open Mihrab on the other device — as soon as it reads the folder, both are paired and syncing.
sync.errorBadCode: Check the code and try again. It is grouped in sixes, and a single wrong character is enough to reject it.
sync.errorThisDevice: That is this device’s own code. You need the one shown on the other device.
sync.errorTooMany: You can pair up to {{max}} devices. Remove one first.
sync.errorSaveBody: The device wouldn’t store it. Try again — nothing was changed.
sync.removeBody: This device will stop sending to it and stop accepting from it. Remove this device on that one too, or it will keep trying.
sync.notReady: This device can’t set up sync: it has no secure source of randomness, and a key made without one would not be private.
sync.privacyNoteP2p: Your code is a public key, not a secret. The data itself is encrypted for your paired devices only, and nothing is uploaded anywhere.
sync.folderHelp: Mihrab doesn't carry the files itself, so any program that syncs a folder between your devices will do — Syncthing, which goes straight from device to device, or a cloud folder such as Nextcloud, OneDrive or Dropbox. Choose a folder it keeps in step on every device; if nothing syncs that folder, nothing reaches your other devices. Mihrab writes one small encrypted file there and reads the ones your other devices left.
sync.autoHelp: Automatic syncs run only while the app is open. Sync now always works, whatever you choose here.
sync.errorFolderGone: That folder can’t be reached any more. Choose it again.
sync.errorUnsupported: This build can’t use folder sync.
sync.syncDoneBody: Everything your other devices had is here now, and what is here is there.
sync.syncNothing: Nothing new. Your other devices haven’t written anything since the last check.

hint.quranTitle: Reading on more than one device?
hint.quranBody: Set up sync and your place, bookmarks and khatmah follow you between them.
hint.logTitle: Log on one device, see it on all of them
hint.logBody: Set up sync to keep your record the same everywhere. Nothing is uploaded.

sync.pairedNeedsFolder: Choose a folder first. That folder is how the two devices reach each other, and until there is one, nothing can be exchanged.
sync.folderAppHint: Mihrab made a folder called {{value}} for itself. Find it in Files, under On My iPhone, and point your sync app at it to reach your other devices.
sync.syncNothingArrived: Your file is in the folder, but nothing from your other devices has appeared there. Both devices have to be pointing at the same folder, and whatever keeps that folder in step between them has to be running.
sync.syncStale: Your file is in the folder, but the newest record from {{device}} was written {{when}}. If you have used that device since, whatever keeps the folder in step between you has stopped carrying files.
sync.scanHint: Point the camera at the code on your other device
sync.scanDeniedBody: Mihrab needs the camera to read the code. You can allow it in your device settings, or type the code in instead.
sync.scanNoCameraBody: This device has no camera to scan with. Type or paste the code instead.
sync.errorFolderUnwritable: That folder can’t be written to. Pick another one — a folder you made yourself in Documents or Downloads works best.

tajweed.title: Tajweed colours
tajweed.settingsBlurb: Tint the letters by their rule, and learn what each colour asks of you
tajweed.toggle: Colour the mushaf by tajweed rule
tajweed.toggleHelp: Letters are tinted in the King Fahd Complex's colours: grey is not sounded, green hums, red stretches, light blue bounces. Turn it on while learning; plain ink is a tap away.
tajweed.warshNote: Tajweed colours are drawn on the Hafs and Warsh mushafs. Switch to one of them to see them.
tajweed.guideIntro: Every tinted letter is a rule at work. One colour is one idea, so a page teaches you as you read: grey is written but not sounded, green is a hum through the nose, the reds are a vowel held longer, light blue is a bounce, and dark blue a heavy letter.
tajweed.guidePractice: To practise: turn the colours on, open any page, and tap an ayah — its sheet lists the rules in it, word by word. Hold a word to hear it read.
tajweed.waiting: After the download that is running
tajweed.queued: Next, after the download that is running · tap to remove
tajweed.downloadAllHelp: Turning the colours on downloads the pages you read in, over Wi-Fi, in the background — it keeps going when you leave this screen or the app. A font carries one palette, so light pages (paper and sepia) and dark pages (night) are two sets of about 170 MB each; on the Auto tone both are fetched.
tajweed.sheetNone: Nothing in this ayah is tinted — no rule applies.
tajweed.sheetUnavailable: The rules for this ayah are not available.

silent.name: Silent
silent.summary: Written, not sounded. The letter is on the page but your tongue passes over it — or it melts into the letter after it.

ghunnah.name: Ghunnah
ghunnah.summary: A hum through the nose, held for about two counts. Every green letter is a nūn or mīm doing this, in one of its forms.

madd.name: Madd
madd.summary: A vowel held longer than usual. The deeper the red, the longer: from two counts up to six.

qalqalah.name: Qalqalah
qalqalah.summary: A small bounce on a still ق ط ب ج د, so the letter is heard and not swallowed.

tafkheem.name: Tafkhīm
tafkheem.summary: A heavy letter, said with the back of the tongue raised: خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ always, the rā after a fatḥah or ḍammah, and the lām of Allah's name after one.

warsh.name: Warsh's own
warsh.summary: What the Warsh reading does differently: a hamza that moves or softens, a vowel leaned towards ē, and a rā that stays light.

ham_wasl.name: Hamzat al-waṣl
ham_wasl.help: The joining alif. It is sounded only when you start on it; joined to the word before, it is skipped.

laam_shamsiyah.name: Sun lām
laam_shamsiyah.help: The lām of ال is not pronounced before a sun letter; that letter is doubled instead.

slnt.name: Silent letter
slnt.help: A letter that is written but never sounded, like the wāw of أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ.

idgham_wo_ghunnah.name: Idghām without ghunnah
idgham_wo_ghunnah.help: A still nūn or tanwīn merges fully into the lām or rā after it, with no hum.

idgham_mutajanisayn.name: Idghām of like letters
idgham_mutajanisayn.help: A still letter merges into the next, which is made in the same place in the mouth — a dāl into a tā.

idgham_mutaqaribayn.name: Idghām of near letters
idgham_mutaqaribayn.help: A still letter merges into a close neighbour — a lām into a rā, a qāf into a kāf.

ghunnah.name: Ghunnah
ghunnah.help: A doubled nūn or mīm is hummed through the nose for two counts.

ikhafa.name: Ikhfāʾ
ikhafa.help: A still nūn or tanwīn is hidden: the tongue does not touch, and a light hum leads into the next letter.

idgham_ghunnah.name: Idghām with ghunnah
idgham_ghunnah.help: A still nūn or tanwīn merges into a following yā, nūn, mīm or wāw, keeping the hum.

iqlab.name: Iqlāb
iqlab.help: A still nūn or tanwīn before a bā turns into a mīm, hummed with the lips lightly closed.

ikhafa_shafawi.name: Ikhfāʾ shafawī
ikhafa_shafawi.help: A still mīm before a bā is hidden with a light hum, the lips barely closed.

idgham_shafawi.name: Idghām shafawī
idgham_shafawi.help: A still mīm merges into the mīm after it, with a hum.

madda_normal.name: Natural madd
madda_normal.help: The plain long vowel: hold it for two counts, no more.

madda_permissible.name: Permissible madd
madda_permissible.help: A long vowel before a pause, or a līn letter: two, four or six counts when you stop on it.

madda_obligatory_mottasel.name: Obligatory connected madd
madda_obligatory_mottasel.help: A long vowel before a hamzah in the same word: hold it four or five counts.

madda_obligatory_monfasel.name: Separated madd
madda_obligatory_monfasel.help: A long vowel at the end of a word before a hamzah starting the next: four or five counts, two when reading fast.

madda_necessary.name: Necessary madd
madda_necessary.help: A long vowel before a sukūn or shaddah that never leaves: hold it six counts. The opening letters of a surah are read this way.

qalaqah.name: Qalqalah
qalaqah.help: A still ق ط ب ج د is given a small bounce so it is clearly heard.

tafkheem.name: Tafkhīm
tafkheem.help: The letter is made heavy, with the back of the tongue raised — always for خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ, and for the rā after a fatḥah or ḍammah and the lām of Allah's name.

madd_badal.name: Madd al-badal
madd_badal.help: A long vowel right after a hamza, as in ءَامَنُواْ. Warsh may hold it for two, four or six counts.

leen_mahmooz.name: Līn before a hamza
leen_mahmooz.help: A still wāw or yā after a fatḥa, with a hamza after it in the same word — شَےْءٖ. Warsh holds it for four or six counts.

laam_taghleedh.name: Heavy lām
laam_taghleedh.help: An open lām after a ṣād, ṭā or ẓā that is open or still is said heavy in Warsh, as in اَ۬لصَّلَوٰةَ.

raa_tarqeeq.name: Light rā
raa_tarqeeq.help: Warsh keeps the rā light after a kasra or a still yā — خَيْرٞ — where Ḥafṣ makes it heavy. Foreign names, a heavy letter after it and a few set words stay heavy.

naql.name: Naql
naql.help: The hamza is dropped and its vowel moves onto the still letter before it: قَدَ اَفْلَحَ is read qada-flaḥa.

tasheel.name: Tashīl
tasheel.help: The second of two hamzas is softened, between a hamza and a long vowel, as in شُهَدَآءَ ا۪ذْ.

taqleel.name: Taqlīl
taqleel.help: The long ā is leaned slightly towards ē, between a fatḥa and an imāla. The small dot below the letter marks it: اَ۬لنَّصَٰر۪ىٰ.

tajweed.turnOn: Show the colours in the mushaf
tajweed.downloadDoneBody: Every coloured page is on this device.

helpMihrab.intro: Mihrab grows by word of mouth. If it has been useful to you, here are three ways to pass it on.
helpMihrab.rateAppStore: Rate it on the App Store
helpMihrab.rateStoreHelp: A rating and a few words help people find it when they search the store.
helpMihrab.rateGithubHelp: A star on GitHub helps people looking for open-source apps find it.
helpMihrab.tellRowHelp: A link to Mihrab's website, which has every way to download it, sent through any app you choose.
helpMihrab.shareMessage: I use Mihrab for prayer times and the Quran. Have a look: {{url}}
helpMihrab.monthRowHelp: This month's prayer times where you are, on one page to send or print.
helpMihrab.monthFooter: Send it to the people you love, or print copies to hand out at your mosque, to family and to neighbours. Every sheet carries Mihrab's address, so whoever it reaches can find the app.
helpMihrab.ratePlayElsewhereHelp: Most people find Mihrab on Google Play. If you have a Google account, a rating there helps, wherever you installed it from.
helpMihrab.homeToggleHelp: The small heart beside the countdown that opens this page.
